scraped.scraped_description: Alaveteli helps you lower the barriers that prevent citizens asking questions of those in power

name: Alaveteli
tagline: Run your own Freedom of Information website - An open-source platform for making public freedom of information requests to public bodies
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
last_funding_event: Ongoing support from mySociety and partner organizations
dependency_risks: Reliance on mySociety for maintenance and development
news_articles: Guardian coverage of FOI campaigns using Alaveteli
Reuters reporting on transparency initiatives powered by Alaveteli
TechCrunch features on civic technology platforms
academic_citations: Citations in academic literature on freedom of information and transparency
Research on civic technology adoption and impact
awards: Recognition as leading open-source civic technology platform
policy_outcomes: Increased FOI request submissions across multiple jurisdictions
Support for investigative journalism and civil society monitoring
Over 1,000,000+ Freedom of Information requests made through platform across 25+ jurisdictions
outcome_methodology: Observational tracking of FOI requests made through platform; user surveys and case studies
published_performance_metrics: 1,000,000+ Freedom of Information requests made across 25+ jurisdictions
documented_limitations: Effectiveness depends on underlying FOI laws in each jurisdiction
Limited data on long-term policy impact from individual requests
Variation in government responsiveness across jurisdictions
jurisdictional_scope: International; supports multiple jurisdictions with customizable FOI processes
failure_modes: Jurisdictions with weak FOI laws limit platform utility
curation_criteria: Open-source contribution guidelines; community-driven feature requests and bug reports through GitHub
contributor_governance: Managed by mySociety with community contributions; transparent issue tracking and pull request process
disparity_tracking: Limited formal tracking; platform aims to democratize access to FOI processes across socioeconomic groups
community_ownership: Community-driven through open-source model; local organizations operate instances in their jurisdictions
government_partnerships: Partnerships with government bodies in multiple jurisdictions to implement FOI request systems
political_relevance_summary: Addresses barriers to meaningful citizen participation in democratic decision-making by providing tools for public engagement and deliberation.

movement_building_utility.notes: Open-source infrastructure that enables others to build or deploy civic technology solutions.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (multiple countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability.
primary_users_or_beneficiaries: citizens seeking to participate in local democratic processes
